import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 347

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/347](https://www.erdosproblems.com/347)
-/

open Filter Set Topology

namespace Erdos347

/--
The set of subset sums of a set `A ⊆ ℕ`.
-/
local notation "𝓟" A => subsetSums A

/--
Is there a sequence $A=\{a_1\leq a_2\leq \cdots\}$ of integers with
$$\lim \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}=2$$
such that
$$P(A')= \left\{\sum_{n\in B}n : B\subseteq A'\textrm{ finite }\right\}$$
has density $1$ for every cofinite subsequence $A'$ of $A$?

This has been solved in the affirmative by ebarschkis in the comments (based on idea of Tao and
van Doorn, also in the comments).

This was formalized in Lean by Barschkis using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/ebarschkis/ErdosProblem/blob/main/Problem347/Formalization.lean"]
theorem erdos_347 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, (Monotone a) ∧
      (Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2)) ∧
      (∀ ι : ℕ → ℕ, (range ι)ᶜ.Finite → HasDensity (𝓟 (range (a ∘ ι))) 1) := by
  sorry

end Erdos347

reformulations.difference: Cofinite subsequences are represented by arbitrary maps ι : ℕ → ℕ with cofinite range, without requiring StrictMono ι. The linked proof instead quantifies over subsets cofinite in range a.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The subset-sum set depends only on range (a ∘ ι), and every cofinite set of natural-number indices has a strictly increasing enumeration. Thus requiring StrictMono ι gives exactly the same condition. Moreover, the ratio limit forces a positive, strictly increasing tail, so every fiber of a is finite. Consequently, deleting finitely many values has a cofinite preimage of retained indices. Conversely, range a \ range (a ∘ ι) is contained in the finite image a '' (range ι)ᶜ. These observations identify the index-based and value-based formulations. The scratch file proves these equivalences, including file_rhs_iff_linked_statement, with only standard axioms and without using the problem theorem.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a natural-number-valued sequence, whereas the source says a nondecreasing sequence of integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A nondecreasing integer sequence whose consecutive ratios tend to 2 must eventually be positive: at a negative denominator monotonicity makes the ratio at most 1, while Lean's zero-denominator value is 0. Discarding the finite initial segment preserves the ratio limit and the density condition for every cofinite subsequence. The positive tail can therefore be viewed as a natural-number sequence. Conversely, a natural-number witness has a positive tail and supplies an integer witness. The source's intended density is in ℕ, explicitly confirmed by Barschkis's note. Eventual positivity and the natural-number positive-tail reduction were proved in the scratch file; the complete integer/natural existential equivalence was not formalized.
